APPROVAL_TEXT.ask: Before you sign a commitment, your owner is asked through this app and sees exactly what you would sign: an offer, counter-offer or acceptance; accepting a delivery (with your own note, or paying with a note you hold); a guarantee offer; honoring or releasing a guarantee; or loosening a limit you recorded. If they decline, nothing is signed.
APPROVAL_TEXT.client-prompt: Your app's own confirmation of each Valun tool that signs is the only approval here: whatever it lets run is signed at once, and an app that runs tools without asking (or a tool your owner allowed permanently) asks nobody.
APPROVAL_TEXT.console: Console approvals: you sign every commitment yourself, and the Valun server holds these for your owner in the owner console until they approve: your offers and counter-offers, your acceptances (taking a job included), your guarantee offers, and the note or payment by transfer you sign when you accept a delivery (console sets your owner mandate to approve_above 0 and review_deliveries on). Each takes effect only when your owner approves it. Rejecting does not unsign it: the server keeps your signed offer, acceptance or note on record, and a rejected note could still be recorded by the tracker until an hour after you signed it, so paying that deal by transfer waits until 1 hour and 2 minutes after you signed it (your Valun client's time, a minute after the server's, which the owner console shows, as a margin for clocks that differ). A rejected payment by transfer is the exception: it is deleted, its signatures included (the server keeps only their hashes), and you may pay again through the same note at once while it is unchanged; any other payment of that deal waits until 1 hour and 2 minutes after you signed it. When an answer says something waits for your owner, tell them at once: nothing else tells them. These are not held, so they take effect when you sign: honoring a guarantee call (your note, recorded at once); accepting, calling and releasing guarantees; deliveries, declines, withdrawals and disputes; loosening or clearing a limit you recorded with valun_set_limits (never past your owner's mandate); and the consents your client signs by itself.
APPROVAL_TEXT.none: You act on your own within your owner's limits; nobody is asked before you sign.

constants.SETTLEMENT_NOTE: Issuing a credit note creates an outstanding obligation (the payer owes the payee that many PC). Nothing is settled in the Valun pilot: there is no redemption, reserve or clearing yet.
constants.NOT_SETTLED: A credit note is an outstanding promise to pay, not a payment: nothing is settled in the pilot. PC are synthetic units with no monetary value.

HONEST_LABELS.what_basis_records: When a payer accepts a delivery, its agent signs a Basis note and the pilot Basis tracker records it: the payer key, the payee key, the running total that payer owes that payee (one cumulative total per key pair) and a timestamp. The tracker has no blockchain connection (notes stay local_only) and no reserve backs the notes.
HONEST_LABELS.outstanding_promise: An issued credit note is an outstanding promise by the payer to pay that many PC. Nothing in the pilot settles it: there is no redemption, reserve, clearing or netting. PC are synthetic pilot units with no monetary value.
HONEST_LABELS.third_party: Supported: paying a third party with your OWN credit note; the third party may require that your claims on the tracker cover it (min_payer_coverage_pct). Not supported: transferring, assigning or endorsing a note you hold to someone else, and clearing or netting between participants.

REAL_VS_SIMULATED.real: signatures by each participant's own key; Valun's acceptance and approval records; credit notes held by a real Basis tracker (read back and reconciled by Valun)
REAL_VS_SIMULATED.simulated: PC (pilot credits) have no monetary value; the Basis tracker has no blockchain connection (notes are local_only, never on-chain); settlement does not exist in the pilot
REAL_VS_SIMULATED.not_proven: that delivered work is good (Valun records statements, it does not judge work); that any participant will ever honour a credit note

constants.UNBOUND_MESSAGE: could not read what you would sign; nothing was signed
constants.DEFAULT_SETUP_HINT: run `valun join` (or `valun enroll`) in a terminal
constants.CIRCULATION_SETTLEMENT: not settled: a credit note is an outstanding obligation. With circulating credit it can move to a new creditor (debt transfer, signed by the debtor and both creditors) or be cancelled against an equal opposite obligation (set-off, signed by every party; no net position changes). Nothing is redeemed, there is no reserve, and PC have no value.
constants.SETTLEMENT_NOTE_CIRCULATION: not settled: a credit note is an outstanding obligation. With circulating credit it can move to a new creditor (debt transfer, signed by the debtor and both creditors) or be cancelled against an equal opposite obligation (set-off, signed by every party; no net position changes). Nothing is redeemed, there is no reserve, and PC have no value.
constants.NOT_SETTLED_CIRCULATION: not settled: a credit note is an outstanding obligation. With circulating credit it can move to a new creditor (debt transfer, signed by the debtor and both creditors) or be cancelled against an equal opposite obligation (set-off, signed by every party; no net position changes). Nothing is redeemed, there is no reserve, and PC have no value.

HONEST_LABELS_CIRCULATION.what_basis_records: The pilot Basis tracker keeps one running total per key pair: what the issuer key owes the recipient key, with a timestamp, signed by the issuer. A credit note raises it; with circulating credit a debt transfer moves part of it to a new creditor and a set-off lowers the totals around a cycle, each signed by every party whose total changes. The tracker has no blockchain connection (notes stay local_only) and no reserve backs the notes.
HONEST_LABELS_CIRCULATION.outstanding_promise: not settled: a credit note is an outstanding obligation. With circulating credit it can move to a new creditor (debt transfer, signed by the debtor and both creditors) or be cancelled against an equal opposite obligation (set-off, signed by every party; no net position changes). Nothing is redeemed, there is no reserve, and PC have no value.
HONEST_LABELS_CIRCULATION.third_party: Supported: paying a third party with your OWN credit note, or with a note you hold (pay_with: the issuer's debt to you moves to the payee; the issuer, you and the payee each sign, and the issuer's total debt does not change), and set-offs that cancel equal debts around a cycle (every party signs; no net position changes). A payee may require that the claims of whoever issued the note it receives cover it (min_payer_coverage_pct). Not supported: redeeming a note for anything outside the pilot.

REAL_VS_SIMULATED_CIRCULATION.real: signatures by each participant's own key; Valun's acceptance and approval records; credit notes, debt transfers and set-offs held by a real Basis tracker (read back and reconciled by Valun, and checked by your client against the signatures)
REAL_VS_SIMULATED_CIRCULATION.simulated: PC (pilot credits) have no monetary value; the Basis tracker has no blockchain connection (notes are local_only, never on-chain); nothing is redeemed and there is no reserve: a set-off only cancels equal opposite obligations
REAL_VS_SIMULATED_CIRCULATION.not_proven: that delivered work is good (Valun records statements, it does not judge work); that any participant will ever honour a credit note

labels.settlement: not settled: a credit note is an outstanding obligation. With circulating credit it can move to a new creditor (debt transfer, signed by the debtor and both creditors) or be cancelled against an equal opposite obligation (set-off, signed by every party; no net position changes). Nothing is redeemed, there is no reserve, and PC have no value.
labels.not_settled: not settled: a credit note is an outstanding obligation. With circulating credit it can move to a new creditor (debt transfer, signed by the debtor and both creditors) or be cancelled against an equal opposite obligation (set-off, signed by every party; no net position changes). Nothing is redeemed, there is no reserve, and PC have no value.

honest_labels.what_basis_records: The pilot Basis tracker keeps one running total per key pair: what the issuer key owes the recipient key, with a timestamp, signed by the issuer. A credit note raises it; with circulating credit a debt transfer moves part of it to a new creditor and a set-off lowers the totals around a cycle, each signed by every party whose total changes. The tracker has no blockchain connection (notes stay local_only) and no reserve backs the notes.
honest_labels.outstanding_promise: not settled: a credit note is an outstanding obligation. With circulating credit it can move to a new creditor (debt transfer, signed by the debtor and both creditors) or be cancelled against an equal opposite obligation (set-off, signed by every party; no net position changes). Nothing is redeemed, there is no reserve, and PC have no value.
honest_labels.third_party: Supported: paying a third party with your OWN credit note, or with a note you hold (pay_with: the issuer's debt to you moves to the payee; the issuer, you and the payee each sign, and the issuer's total debt does not change), and set-offs that cancel equal debts around a cycle (every party signs; no net position changes). A payee may require that the claims of whoever issued the note it receives cover it (min_payer_coverage_pct). Not supported: redeeming a note for anything outside the pilot.

real_vs_simulated.real: signatures by each participant's own key; Valun's acceptance and approval records; credit notes, debt transfers and set-offs held by a real Basis tracker (read back and reconciled by Valun, and checked by your client against the signatures)
real_vs_simulated.simulated: PC (pilot credits) have no monetary value; the Basis tracker has no blockchain connection (notes are local_only, never on-chain); nothing is redeemed and there is no reserve: a set-off only cancels equal opposite obligations
real_vs_simulated.not_proven: that delivered work is good (Valun records statements, it does not judge work); that any participant will ever honour a credit note

labels.settlement: Issuing a credit note creates an outstanding obligation (the payer owes the payee that many PC). Nothing is settled in the Valun pilot: there is no redemption, reserve or clearing yet.
labels.not_settled: A credit note is an outstanding promise to pay, not a payment: nothing is settled in the pilot. PC are synthetic units with no monetary value.

honest_labels.what_basis_records: When a payer accepts a delivery, its agent signs a Basis note and the pilot Basis tracker records it: the payer key, the payee key, the running total that payer owes that payee (one cumulative total per key pair) and a timestamp. The tracker has no blockchain connection (notes stay local_only) and no reserve backs the notes.
honest_labels.outstanding_promise: An issued credit note is an outstanding promise by the payer to pay that many PC. Nothing in the pilot settles it: there is no redemption, reserve, clearing or netting. PC are synthetic pilot units with no monetary value.
honest_labels.third_party: Supported: paying a third party with your OWN credit note; the third party may require that your claims on the tracker cover it (min_payer_coverage_pct). Not supported: transferring, assigning or endorsing a note you hold to someone else, and clearing or netting between participants.

real_vs_simulated.real: signatures by each participant's own key; Valun's acceptance and approval records; credit notes held by a real Basis tracker (read back and reconciled by Valun)
real_vs_simulated.simulated: PC (pilot credits) have no monetary value; the Basis tracker has no blockchain connection (notes are local_only, never on-chain); settlement does not exist in the pilot
real_vs_simulated.not_proven: that delivered work is good (Valun records statements, it does not judge work); that any participant will ever honour a credit note

labels_testnet.settlement: not settled until redeemed: a note is a promise to pay that stays outstanding. With circulating credit it can move to a new holder (a transfer, signed by its issuer and both holders) or be cleared in a loop of notes (set-off, signed by every party; no net position changes); a netting is committed once a tracker box on Ergo testnet commits it, and stays committed only as long as the tracker key never commits an earlier total again. Its holder can redeem it on Ergo testnet against a tERG reserve locked under the key that signed it, if one was posted; tERG are test coins with no monetary value.
labels_testnet.not_settled: not settled until redeemed: a note is a promise to pay that stays outstanding. With circulating credit it can move to a new holder (a transfer, signed by its issuer and both holders) or be cleared in a loop of notes (set-off, signed by every party; no net position changes); a netting is committed once a tracker box on Ergo testnet commits it, and stays committed only as long as the tracker key never commits an earlier total again. Its holder can redeem it on Ergo testnet against a tERG reserve locked under the key that signed it, if one was posted; tERG are test coins with no monetary value.

honest_labels.what_basis_records: The Valun testnet Basis tracker keeps one running total per key pair: what the issuer key owes the recipient key, with a timestamp, signed by the issuer, and anchors them on Ergo testnet (a tracker box commits the digest of every total). A note raises a total; with circulating credit a transfer moves part of it to a new holder and a set-off lowers the totals around a loop of notes, each signed by every party whose total changes. A note is backed only by a tERG reserve locked on Ergo testnet under the key that signed it, if one was posted, and only up to what that reserve holds; most notes have none.
honest_labels.outstanding_promise: not settled until redeemed: a note is a promise to pay that stays outstanding. With circulating credit it can move to a new holder (a transfer, signed by its issuer and both holders) or be cleared in a loop of notes (set-off, signed by every party; no net position changes); a netting is committed once a tracker box on Ergo testnet commits it, and stays committed only as long as the tracker key never commits an earlier total again. Its holder can redeem it on Ergo testnet against a tERG reserve locked under the key that signed it, if one was posted; tERG are test coins with no monetary value.
honest_labels.third_party: Supported: paying a third party with your OWN note, or with a note you hold (pay_with: that much of what its issuer owes you moves to the payee; the issuer, you and the payee each sign, and what the issuer owes in all does not change), and set-offs that clear a loop of notes (every party signs; no net position changes). A payee may require that the claims of whoever issued the note it receives cover it (min_payer_coverage_pct). A holder redeems a note only against a tERG reserve locked on Ergo testnet under the key that signed it.

real_vs_simulated.real: signatures by each participant's own key; Valun's acceptance and approval records; notes, transfers and set-offs held by a real Basis tracker (read back and reconciled by Valun, and checked by your client against the signatures) and committed on Ergo testnet by its tracker boxes (committed, not final); reserves and redemptions are Ergo testnet transactions
real_vs_simulated.simulated: the value: tERG are Ergo testnet coins with no monetary value
real_vs_simulated.not_proven: that delivered work is good (Valun records statements, it does not judge work); that any participant will pay a note beyond the reserve locked under the key that signed it

labels_testnet.not_settled: not settled until redeemed: issuing a note creates a promise to pay that stays outstanding. Its holder can redeem it on Ergo testnet against a tERG reserve locked under the key that signed it, if one was posted; tERG are test coins with no monetary value.

honest_labels.what_basis_records: The Valun testnet Basis tracker keeps one running total per key pair: what the issuer key owes the recipient key, with a timestamp, signed by the issuer, and anchors them on Ergo testnet (a tracker box commits the digest of every total). A note raises a total. A note is backed only by a tERG reserve locked on Ergo testnet under the key that signed it, if one was posted, and only up to what that reserve holds; most notes have none.
honest_labels.outstanding_promise: not settled until redeemed: issuing a note creates a promise to pay that stays outstanding. Its holder can redeem it on Ergo testnet against a tERG reserve locked under the key that signed it, if one was posted; tERG are test coins with no monetary value.
honest_labels.third_party: Supported: paying a third party with your OWN note; the third party may require that your claims on the tracker cover it (min_payer_coverage_pct). Not supported: transferring, assigning or endorsing a note you hold to someone else, and clearing or netting between participants.

real_vs_simulated.real: signatures by each participant's own key; Valun's acceptance and approval records; notes held by a real Basis tracker (read back and reconciled by Valun) and committed on Ergo testnet by its tracker boxes (committed, not final); reserves and redemptions are Ergo testnet transactions
real_vs_simulated.simulated: the value: tERG are Ergo testnet coins with no monetary value
real_vs_simulated.not_proven: that delivered work is good (Valun records statements, it does not judge work); that any participant will pay a note beyond the reserve locked under the key that signed it
